title: MobileSteward: Integrating Multiple App-Oriented Agents with Self-Evolution to Automate Cross-App Instructions

problem.claim: Automating complex cross-app instructions on mobile phones.

gap.claim: Existing procedure-oriented agents struggle with complex task relationships, diverse app environments, and error propagation or information loss during multi-step execution.

contributions.claim: MobileSteward is a self-evolving multi-agent framework that integrates multiple app-oriented StaffAgents coordinated by a centralized StewardAgent.

The framework includes Dynamic Recruitment, Assigned Execution, and Adjusted Evaluation to associate cross-app tasks, assign app-specialized agents, and mitigate error propagation or information loss.
A Memory-based Self-evolution mechanism summarizes successful execution experience to improve MobileSteward's performance.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experimental results report that MobileSteward achieves the best performance compared with single-agent and multi-agent frameworks.
The reported results highlight better handling of user instructions with diverse complexity.

narrative_sequence.summary: Mobile phone agents are presented as useful for automating daily tasks.
Existing procedure-oriented agents face challenges in cross-app instruction execution.
MobileSteward addresses the challenges through coordinated app-oriented agents and three specialized execution modules.
Memory-based self-evolution uses successful execution experience for continuous improvement.
CAPBench is introduced and experiments report strong comparative performance.

source_observation.claim: Cross-app execution involves complex task relationships, diverse app environments, and error propagation or information loss across multiple steps.

interpretation.claim: Separating coordination, app-specific execution, and evaluation may help manage distinct sources of cross-app complexity.

application.claim: For other multi-system automation settings, use explicit dependency-aware coordination, specialized workers, and feedback during execution.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this decomposition benefits tasks outside the described mobile cross-app setting.

source_observation.claim: The framework summarizes experience from successful executions to improve subsequent performance.

interpretation.claim: Experience-driven self-evolution may provide a way to improve agent behavior without changing the overall multi-agent structure.

application.claim: Automation systems could retain and summarize successful execution experience for future adaptation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the memory contents, update procedure, or conditions under which self-evolution is effective.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide quantitative results, baselines, datasets beyond CAPBench, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not describe the scheduling graph, agent coordination protocol, evaluation procedure, or self-evolution implementation details.
The abstract does not report limitations, failure cases, resource costs, or reproducibility details.
